requirements.text: Keep the footer, and make its toggle behave the same as the sidebar's Ctrl+B toggle so the two stay in step.

Add a command palette that lists every app-level command the app offers - the global commands and the commands that exist only while an app is open - each with its real shortcut or a clear 'No shortcut' note, so any command hidden from the default view can still be found and run by typing its name, and a query that matches no command shows an empty result. Controls that stay always visible and act on the current view or on data - the editor's own file commands (Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+N new, Ctrl+O open), the Shell and theme choices, the branch choice, app and terminal rows and context-specific dialog answers - are not app-level commands and stay on their visible controls instead of being listed as palette commands.

Every optional tool the user has opened in an app view that this revision makes hideable - the git tools (collapsing back to the branch chip), the git drawer (its Close control) and the console (a new Hide console control) - can be hidden again on demand, so after prolonged use the user can return to the calm default view without restarting the app. Hiding the console selects a terminal in the same app and leaves the console's xterm mounted and running, so its output stays available for the rest of the session. Hiding is offered whenever it leaves a usable workspace; when a console is the only workspace (an app with no terminals), its Hide console control is shown disabled with a visible reason instead of leaving a blank screen. A Reset layout command hides, never closes, the visible optional tools and returns the sidebar, git tools, git drawer and a hideable console to the calm default. Banners (folder lock, job warning, update, manual-update result, error), dialogs and terminal panes are not part of this hide cycle: they keep their existing close and dismiss controls, and Reset layout does not close them or discard unsaved input.

Remember the window's layout between sessions so the user does not have to rearrange the screen each time: the sidebar's expanded or collapsed state is saved when the app closes and restored when it reopens, and the plan lists any other window-level layout fields it saves, none of which may put an optional tool on screen. Opening an app always starts from the calm default view - its git tools collapsed, its git drawer closed and its console hidden - so a previous session's open drawer or console is never reopened just by opening the app, and the earlier promise that an app shows neither the git tools nor the console until the user asks for them still holds. A first run, or an unreadable or inapplicable saved layout, starts in the default minimal view, and restoring the layout never restarts terminals or restores old output.

Build the new UI building blocks from reliable, free, openly licensed, actively maintained npm packages confirmed to work with React 18.3 inside the Tauri webview, instead of hand-rolling them: the command palette, shortcut handling, menus, dialogs and collapsible panes each use an established package where a suitable one exists. House-rule jattac libraries are preferred where they perform the same function and can be used as published; where a jattac package cannot be used as published, the plan records why and uses a maintained alternative or a stated in-house choice. Anything built in-house is a stated choice with a reason.

Characterization tests before the palette package swap and the new hide controls. The palette, footer, console list and git chip are merged code (USR-004) and this revision changes their internals and controls; freezing what they do today keeps filtering, the empty result, choose-then-run, Escape, the footer's current content and the chip/console behaviour from changing silently.

Reuse the existing sidebar preference instead of a new layout record. R9 only needs the window-level sidebar state, and the sidebar's collapsed flag is already saved under td.sidebarCollapsed with a safe fallback, so keeping that key avoids a migration and makes it impossible to restore an app's git drawer or console at startup.
Keep the footer, and make its toggle behave the same as the sidebar's Ctrl+B toggle so the two stay in step.

R6: shows the footer toggle in its collapsed state when the sidebar is collapsed
R6: the footer stays above optional parts: the toggle is rendered beside the version, never instead of it
R6: the footer toggle and Ctrl+B move the sidebar together and stay in step
R6: a saved collapsed sidebar shows the footer toggle collapsed on the next start
R6: the footer toggle and Ctrl+B still agree while an app view has focus
R6: the footer toggle and Ctrl+B keep the sidebar and footer in step, and the footer stays while tools are hidden

A2: opening an app reads no saved drawer or console state and only the sidebar key is written

requirements.text: Keep the footer, and make its toggle behave the same as the sidebar's Ctrl+B toggle so the two stay in step.
tests: R6: the footer toggle and Ctrl+B move the sidebar together and stay in step
R6: a saved collapsed sidebar shows the footer toggle collapsed on the next start
R6: the footer toggle and Ctrl+B keep the sidebar and footer in step, and the footer stays while tools are hidden
R6: the footer toggle and Ctrl+B still agree while an app view has focus
R6: keeps one sidebar toggle that reads and reports the shared sidebar state
R6: shows the footer toggle in its collapsed state when the sidebar is collapsed
R6: the footer stays above optional parts: the toggle is rendered beside the version, never instead of it

requirements.text: Add a command palette that lists every app-level command the app offers - the global commands and the commands that exist only while an app is open - each with its real shortcut or a clear 'No shortcut' note, so any command hidden from the default view can still be found and run by typing its name, and a query that matches no command shows an empty result. Controls that stay always visible and act on the current view or on data - the editor's own file commands (Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+N new, Ctrl+O open), the Shell and theme choices, the branch choice, app and terminal rows and context-specific dialog answers - are not app-level commands and stay on their visible controls instead of being listed as palette commands.
tests: R7: the palette lists app-level commands and shows an empty result when a query matches none
R4/R7: the editor keeps Ctrl+S, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+O and Ctrl+W while it has focus
R7: the palette lists every app-level command with its real shortcut or no shortcut, and app-only ones only while an app is open
R7: a query that matches no command shows an empty result
R7: typing a hidden command's name finds it and runs it
R7/R8: the palette hides and reopens the git tools, the git drawer and the console
A1/R7: keeps the name filter and the 'No commands match.' empty result
R7: every app-level command shows its real shortcut or a clear No shortcut note
R7/R8: a command that cannot run now is listed disabled with a visible reason and never runs

requirements.text: Every optional tool the user has opened in an app view that this revision makes hideable - the git tools (collapsing back to the branch chip), the git drawer (its Close control) and the console (a new Hide console control) - can be hidden again on demand, so after prolonged use the user can return to the calm default view without restarting the app. Hiding the console selects a terminal in the same app and leaves the console's xterm mounted and running, so its output stays available for the rest of the session. Hiding is offered whenever it leaves a usable workspace; when a console is the only workspace (an app with no terminals), its Hide console control is shown disabled with a visible reason instead of leaving a blank screen. A Reset layout command hides, never closes, the visible optional tools and returns the sidebar, git tools, git drawer and a hideable console to the calm default. Banners (folder lock, job warning, update, manual-update result, error), dialogs and terminal panes are not part of this hide cycle: they keep their existing close and dismiss controls, and Reset layout does not close them or discard unsaved input.
tests: R8: Reset layout returns the calm default without stopping a running terminal
R8: hiding the git drawer keeps an in-progress commit message when it is reopened
R8: a console that is the only workspace cannot be hidden, so Reset layout leaves it on screen
R8: Reset layout leaves banners without a Dismiss action on screen
R8: Reset layout does not close an app edit form or discard its unsaved input
R5/R8: an app view starts with the git tools collapsed behind the branch chip and they hide again on demand
R8: the palette hides a running console without stopping it, and showing it again keeps it running
R7/R8: the palette hides and reopens the git tools, the git drawer and the console
R8: Hide console hides it without stopping it, and showing it again keeps the same running shell
R7/R8: a command that cannot run now is listed disabled with a visible reason and never runs
R8: a controlled caller collapses the tools from the chip and decides the new state
R8: Hide console hides it without closing, and is disabled with a visible reason when it is the only workspace

requirements.text: Remember the window's layout between sessions so the user does not have to rearrange the screen each time: the sidebar's expanded or collapsed state is saved when the app closes and restored when it reopens, and the plan lists any other window-level layout fields it saves, none of which may put an optional tool on screen. Opening an app always starts from the calm default view - its git tools collapsed, its git drawer closed and its console hidden - so a previous session's open drawer or console is never reopened just by opening the app, and the earlier promise that an app shows neither the git tools nor the console until the user asks for them still holds. A first run, or an unreadable or inapplicable saved layout, starts in the default minimal view, and restoring the layout never restarts terminals or restores old output.
tests: R9: the sidebar state survives a restart and a corrupt saved value falls back to the calm default
R9: an unreadable saved layout does not stop the app and starts expanded
R9: a console open at close is not restarted and its old output is not restored
R9: a dialog, branch menu, theme finder, edit form and banner open at close are not reopened on restart
R9: opening an app restores only the sidebar state and starts with the git drawer and console hidden
R9: switching between apps does not show the console or git drawer a previous visit left open

requirements.text: Build the new UI building blocks from reliable, free, openly licensed, actively maintained npm packages confirmed to work with React 18.3 inside the Tauri webview, instead of hand-rolling them: the command palette, shortcut handling, menus, dialogs and collapsible panes each use an established package where a suitable one exists. House-rule jattac libraries are preferred where they perform the same function and can be used as published; where a jattac package cannot be used as published, the plan records why and uses a maintained alternative or a stated in-house choice. Anything built in-house is a stated choice with a reason.
tests: R10: the palette uses the pinned cmdk package, loaded on demand and never with the initial view
R10: the plan records each building block's package or in-house choice with licence, maintenance and React 18.3 compatibility, and the jattac fallback
